data.method_source: send_files whole-corpus batch (Shashi rr_app.py:179, Leela rr_driver.py:331); basename attribution Leela rr_driver.py:91-93; basis-field pattern Shashi rr_app.py:181-188

submission_shape.client_concurrency_note: send_files(files, token) takes no concurrency argument — the SDK docstring says 'Server handles queuing automatically'. C is not a client variable on this arm; the engine's pool decides and is not observable from here.

throughput.basis: MEASURED — one call, one return, wall clock around it

time_to_first_result.basis: batch websocket API — send_files returns all documents at once, so the first observable result IS the batch completion (Shashi rr_app.py:186-188)

client_observed.basis: NOT AVAILABLE. One submit, one return: per-document client instants do not exist under a batched send.

upload_time_derived.basis: BATCH-POSITION latency: upload_time classified as a completion OFFSET from batch open, so these percentiles INCLUDE queue wait inside the batch. Comparable with Leela's derived column (his completion_ns = t0 + upload_time is the same reading); NOT service latency and NOT comparable with the per-document arm's measured column.

engine_side_concurrency.basis: sum(upload_time)/wall, valid ONLY under duration semantics. Classification: offset — fits offset only at seconds (SDK data.py docstring: '{upload_time:.2f}s'): max ~= wall (last completion is the batch return) while sum exceeds the pool ceiling

upload_time_semantics.reason: fits offset only at seconds (SDK data.py docstring: '{upload_time:.2f}s'): max ~= wall (last completion is the batch return) while sum exceeds the pool ceiling

attribution.method: filepath basename (Leela rr_driver.py:91-93), never list position

census_policy.subset_basis: throughput and gates rest on the 9886-document extracted subset; 89 empty documents are reported, not failures
census_policy.hard_loss_note: no_response_for_file and transport errors fail REGARDLESS of policy — lost work always fails

engine.note: measured exposure on stock 3.3.1, our corpus: 5/199 documents at repeat_factor 2. self_duplication must read 0 on a patched build.

provenance.threads_note: threads_requested is what use() was ASKED for; the engine's realised pool size is not observable from the client. Requested != activated != effective cores — the last of those is measured from the CPU sampler and reported under achieved_parallelism.
provenance.warm_up_policy_open_question: OPEN FOR THE GROUP, not resolved here. Leela warms 25 documents taken from BEYOND the measured set (matched_run.sh WARM=25, rr_driver.py:244 all_pdfs[n:n+warm_docs]). Shashi warms max(4, 2*threads) for blast and 2 for sequential, on files[:warm_n] — i.e. the FIRST MEASURED DOCUMENTS, which are then measured cache-hot while their peers are cold. The policies differ in COUNT and in DISJOINTNESS. We use Leela's 25 disjoint because disjointness is a correctness property while the count is a tuning knob, but this is a divergence neither teammate has flagged and it needs a group decision.

projection_to_10k.basis: linear extrapolation from n=9975 at 5176.5s (0.524s/doc). OPTIMISTIC: assumes the batch scheduler does not degrade with queue depth. Compare against SMOKE_BATCH_TIMEOUT_S=36000s.
